request.topic: AI-assisted payment attacks: verify authorization where money actually moves
request.audience: Business and IT leaders responsible for payment systems
request.objective: An approval record alone is insufficient evidence that authorization holds at the point of payment execution. Leaders should trace the approved decision through to the final transfer. Write 140-180 words; keep the argument and factual limits fixed, with no sales CTA or generic engagement question.

evidence.title: S1 / C1: CERT-In update, November4,2026
evidence.fact: CERT-In reports an AI-assisted campaign targeting Indian financial entities through their payment interfaces.

evidence.title: S2 / C2: CERT-In CIAD-2026-0046, October9,2026
evidence.fact: The earlier advisory describes stolen credentials enabling direct payment calls that bypass application checks, and recommends binding transaction stages and validating payouts against approved records.

style_traits.rhythm: Mostly brief declarative sentences and compact paragraphs. Use a deliberate pause or a longer sentence only when it earns its space.
style_traits.reasoning: Expose one questionable assumption with a precise question or compact claim. Let the implication do the persuading; avoid explaining the same point twice.
style_traits.imagery: One economical concrete comparison may help; ornament and dramatic scenes are unnecessary.
style_traits.preferred_structure: A compact question or claim, a tightly reasoned implication, and an earned challenge. Place the factual anchor where the reasoning needs it; do not default to a news-summary paragraph.
